data.gender_notes: Tilak is used as a unisex name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: A mark or sign, especially one made by applying a powder or vermilion to the forehead of a Hindu as a symbol of devotion or blessing. The name Tilak carries the meaning “Mark, Sign” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Hindu tradition and is also used in Sanskrit, Hindi. Parents who choose Tilak usually hope their child will grow to embody mark, sign and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: A sacred mark or symbol, representing the divine presence or protection.
data.etymology: Tilak belongs to the Hindu linguistic tradition and is used in Hindu naming. Its recorded meaning is “Mark, Sign.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Tilak total 8, giving a life-path number of 8. Number 8 is linked with Saturn and with the qualities of ambition, resilience and material success.

data.cultural_impact: The Hindu custom of wearing a Tilak, or a sacred mark, on the forehead is deeply rooted in Indian culture and traditions. These marks are often made with sandal or turmeric paste, ashes, or vermilion powder, and represent various spiritual and worldly virtues or deities. Wearing a Tilak is a way to affirm one's identity as a Hindu, and it is also a symbol of respect and reverence for the gods and generational traditions. The practice has been widespread among Hindus for centuries, and it continues to be an important part of daily life for many.
data.spiritual_significance: The Hindu Tilak also holds deep spiritual significance. It serves as a reminder of the presence of the divine within oneself and is believed to protect the wearer from evil and negative energies. Wearing a Tilak is a way to invoke the blessings of the deities and to dedicate oneself to the spiritual path. The practice of applying a Tilak is often accompanied by mantras or prayers, adding an additional layer of spiritual meaning to the ritual. The various colors and forms of the Tilak symbolize different deities or virtues, further emphasizing the spiritual dimension of this tradition.
data.spiritual_symbolism: The tilak is a mark of Shiva's blessing, symbolizing the third eye of wisdom and protection. It signifies the individual's connection to the divine and their inner awakening.

vedic_reference.note: The name Tilak is derived from the Sanskrit word tilaka, which means 'mark, symbol, or sign made by applying a powder or paste on the forehead.' In Hindu mythology, tilaka is applied as a symbol of protection and blessing from the gods.
